The khăn rằn, known for its intricate black and white patterns, is typically worn around the neck or draped over the shoulders, symbolizing cultural identity and pride in Vietnamese heritage. Originating in the Mekong Delta region of southern Vietnam, the khăn rằn has a rich history dating back to the 19th century when it was adapted from the Cambodian krama and used as a practical item for both protection and identification. During the Vietnam War, the khăn rằn became a powerful symbol of resistance and identity for National Liberation Front soldiers. Today, the khăn rằn continues to be an important cultural symbol, often seen during traditional festivals and worn by locals to express their pride in their cultural heritage.
